# implicit-sdf.library: ComplementDistance

**Status:** Supported (tier `geometry`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

> The complement of a shape: inside becomes outside, and the magnitude is
> unchanged, so an exact operand stays exact. This is the one CSG operator
> with no meaningful BOUNDED form — the complement of a bounded solid is
> unbounded, so no conservative box can enclose its non-positive region,
> which is why there is no Complement beside the Union / Intersection /
> Difference wrappers above.

## Signature

```plato
ComplementDistance(a: Number): Number
```

## Laws

These are declared laws. Whether each one passes is recorded by the law runner ([stdlib/VERIFICATION.md](../../../../../stdlib/VERIFICATION.md)), not by this page.

### Law_ComplementIsInvolution

[stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato, line 249](../../../../../stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato#L249)

```plato
// Complementing twice is the identity.
Law_ComplementIsInvolution(a: Number): Boolean
    => ComplementDistance(ComplementDistance(a)).LawEq(a);
```

### Law_SubtractIsIntersectWithComplementOperator

[stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato, line 254](../../../../../stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato#L254)

```plato
// Difference is intersection against a complement, stated through the operator
// rather than through raw negation.
Law_SubtractIsIntersectWithComplementOperator(a: Number, b: Number): Boolean
    => SubtractDistance(a, b).LawEq(IntersectionDistance(a, ComplementDistance(b)));
```
